gaps: The Academia Sinica text view records a bronze-inscription item for 關 but does not display a glyph or date the inscription; no glyph image was visually inspected. Earliest securely datable graphic attestation remains unresolved from accessed text.

The claim that the bronze form depicts two sticks locking a door is reported by Wiktionary, but its actual graphic evidence and interpretation could not be checked against a visible inscription image. The name/pronunciation of the hypothesized depicted object is unrecovered, so an object-name-based whole-graph phonetic loan is unsupported.

The phonetic component 𢇅 is identified by the Shuowen and attributed modern accounts, but its exact form-history and independent historical pronunciation comparison were not established by inspected source pages. The character’s own Baxter–Sagart readings are supplied; no matching reconstruction for 𢇅 was verified here.

關關 in the Classic of Poetry is an early literary bird-call expression, but whether this is a use of the same lexical root as ‘barrier’ or a distinct sound word/loan is unresolved. A pronoun-like or bird-call reconstruction alone cannot establish the depicted object’s name.

The semantic passage from crossbar/door fastener to shutting, frontier passes, mechanisms, involvement, and relation is supported by dictionary examples and commentary, but individual transitions are not all demonstrated by dated intermediate attestations in the inspected sources.

The textual record verified 1956 simplification standardization but did not establish the precise graphic source for 关 or prove derivation from 関. Treat the dossier’s competing simplification explanations as unresolved.

A contemporary Simplified Mandarin and Cantonese reading for 关 is not separately attested in the inspected external source; the listed readings directly concern 關, whose conventional simplified correspondence is 关.

The entry-specific Xiaoxuetang query for 關 was inaccessible through the web tool, so no exact Xiaoxuetang image URL or label could be verified. The general CC0 notice was inspected, but it does not license an unverified candidate image.

CUHK’s 關 entry reports eleven bronze-script and two seal-script glyph examples, but its linked direct image pages returned no readable contents. Since no direct image URL and provenance record could be verified from the inspected page output, no glyph image is proposed.

No image was visually inspected. The CUHK and Ministry records support candidate forms and textual descriptions only; they do not establish an image candidate’s pixel content or exact artifact identity.
The bronze analysis has competing explanations for 卝 and other components; the inspected page does not settle whether these forms depict a door lock, encode sound, or represent an earlier graph.
The proposed sound role of 𢇅 is supported here as a 說文 assertion. The inspected sources did not provide an independently checked historical pronunciation for 𢇅 to compare with 關.
The bronze-period pass attestation is cited by the CUHK database, but the page inspected does not date that specific inscription; a precise first-attestation date is unresolved.
